step1_figure.description: A higher performance level-sensitive latch that uses a transmission gate (TG) at the input and another TG in the feedback loop. This prevents the input from fighting the feedback inverter, improving noise performance and reducing contention current.

delay_d_to_q.description: Propagation delay from the D input to the Q output when the latch is transparent (clock is high).

equation.explanation: The delay is determined by the effective switching resistance of the transmission gate and inverters charging/discharging the node capacitances.
equation.assumptions: Linear RC approximation for gate delay.

sky130_expected.calculation: For a minimum sized inverter in SKY130, R_eq ~ 3.6 kOhm. C_load ~ 2-5 fF. Delay per stage ~ 0.7 * 3.6k * 3fF ~ 7.5ps. With 3 stages (TG + 2 inverters) and parasitics, expect ~50-150ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on typical FO1 delays in 130nm CMOS (30-50ps per stage).

setup_time.description: Minimum time the D input must be stable before the clock transitions low to correctly capture the data.

equation.explanation: The data must propagate through the input transmission gate and the first inverter to settle on the internal node before the clock edge is applied.
equation.assumptions: Clock edge is instantaneous and TG turns off immediately.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay through TG and first inverter. ~2 stages * 30ps = 60ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Setup time is roughly the propagation delay to the internal storage node.

hold_time.description: Minimum time the D input must be held stable after the clock transitions low.

equation.explanation: Because of the propagation delay from D to the internal node, the input can be removed slightly before the clock pulse is applied, yielding a negative hold time.
equation.assumptions: Transmission gate turns off faster than the D signal propagates.

sky130_expected.calculation: TG turn-off time minus D-to-internal delay. Typically negative.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard behavior for this latch topology in modern processes.

metastability_delay.description: Time required for the cross-coupled inverters to resolve to a valid logic level when starting from a metastable state (VDD/2).

equation.explanation: Resolution time depends on the time constant of the cross-coupled inverters and the initial voltage offset from the switching point.

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends heavily on initial offset. For a 1mV offset, resolution takes a few time constants. Time constant ~ R_eq * C_node ~ 10ps. ln(1V/1mV) ~ 7. 7 * 10ps ~ 70ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Simulations typically show 100-500ps depending on node capacitance and initial offset.

input_capacitance.description: Capacitance seen at the D input.

equation.explanation: Input capacitance is dominated by the gate capacitance of the transistors in the transmission gate and first inverter.
equation.assumptions: Miller effect is negligible during initial transition.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on typical gate oxide capacitance for 130nm.

step3_testbench.description: Measures propagation delay, setup time, and metastability resolution time for the level-sensitive latch.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Level-Sensitive Latch Testbench
.lib ${SKY130_PDK} tt

* Parameters for the DUT
.param W_xm1=1 L_xm1=0.15
.param W_xm2=2 L_xm2=0.15
.param W_xm5=1 L_xm5=0.15
.param W_xm6=2 L_xm6=0.15
.param W_xm7=1 L_xm7=0.15
.param W_xm3=2 L_xm3=0.15
.param W_xm4=1 L_xm4=0.15
.param W_xm8=2 L_xm8=0.15

* --- DUT Netlist ---
xm1 Q_bar N001 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm2 Q_bar N001 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm5 Q Q_bar 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
xm6 Q Q_bar VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
xm7 D clock N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm7} l={L_xm7}
xm3 N001 clock_b D VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 N001 clock_b Q 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm8 Q clock N001 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
Vclock1 clock_b 0 DC 0.9
* -------------------

* Additional Sources for Testbench
Vclock clock 0 DC 1.8
VD D 0 PULSE(0 1.8 100p 10p 10p 1n 2n)

.control
* 1. Measure Propagation Delay and Setup Time
* Make latch transparent (clock=1.8, clock_b=0)
alter Vclock1 dc = 0
tran 1p 3n
meas tran delay_d_to_q trig v(d) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(q) val=0.9 rise=1
meas tran setup_time trig v(d) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(q_bar) val=0.9 fall=1

* 2. Measure Metastability Delay
* Put latch in hold mode (clock=0, clock_b=1.8)
alter Vclock dc = 0
alter Vclock1 dc = 1.8
* Force internal nodes to metastable state with 1mV offset
ic v(n001)=0.901 v(q_bar)=0.899 v(q)=0.901
tran 1p 2n uic
meas tran metastability_delay trig time val=0 targ v(q) val=1.7 rise=1

quit
.endc
.end
